documents.title: Salt Scales Syndicate — Trade Ledger, Quarter 3
documents.author: Harlan Q., Syndicate Account-Keeper
documents.text: Brine water, 440L issued to Holdfast caravan (receipt #1147). Bone ash, 12 kg returned short — carrier denies. Iodine pills, 30 units traded at 4:1 against filtered charcoal. Net deficit on the quarter: 18 litres of distillate. Note: the caravan master's scales read 2% heavy. I have said nothing. The discrepancy funds the relay station repairs at Lock Gate Four. The ledger balances when the ledger wants to balance.

documents.title: Unsent Letter — Forward Roster Camp, Envelope Sealed
documents.author: Private Colm V.
documents.text: Maren — I am writing this and I will not send it because the courier line is for orders and the orders do not go south. The food is the same every day. I do not mind the food. I mind the sound the wind makes through the checkpoint wire at night. It sounds like someone humming a song they do not remember. Tell the boy his father still has the button. I still have the button. I will bring the button. I am saving the button.

documents.title: Pump Station Nine — Weekly Maintenance Log, Week 14
documents.author: Shift Tech Arek
documents.text: Mon: Impeller seal replaced. Old seal was cracked — 6 months past rated life. No spares left after this one. Tue: Intake pressure dropping. 2.1 bar, down from 2.8. Possible blockage upstream. Wed: Blockage confirmed. Sediment buildup at 40m. Cleared by hand. Took 3 hours. Thu: Nothing. Fri: Intake pressure still low. 2.0 bar. Sat: Borrowed a seal from Station 7 backup. Do not tell Station 7. Sun: Pressure stable at 2.6. Will hold until the next seal cracks. There are no more seals.

documents.title: Ward B Ration Allocation Ledger — Month 6
documents.author: Quartermaster's Office (copy)
documents.text: WARD B — MONTHLY ALLOCATION, MONTH 6. Headcount: 38 (34 active, 2 bedridden, 2 children). Flour: 76 kg (2 kg/person/week × 38 × 1 week reserve). Protein block: 19 kg (500 g/person/week × 38). Fuel oil: 12L (heating only, night cycle). Brine water: 190L (5L/person/week × 38). DEFICIT NOTE: Flour short 8 kg against request. Protein block short 4.5 kg. Substitution: dried fish at 1:1 ratio approved. Residents of Ward B have filed three complaints regarding substitution. Complaints are on file. The fish is the protein. The fish is adequate.

documents.title: Reconnaissance Field Report — Eastern Road Corridor
documents.author: Scout Lead Dara K.
documents.text: Party of four. Departed shelter gate Day 155, 0600. Route: eastern road toward the railway span. Observations: Road surface degraded — cratering at 2 km intervals consistent with airburst overpressure, not ground impact. Radiation nominal at 1.2 mSv/hr surface. Vegetation showing sparse recovery in the drainage ditches (grass, 10–15 cm). No human contact. At 6 km: collapsed overpass, impassable. Turned back. Reached shelter gate Day 158, 1740. Recommendation: eastern corridor is walkable but offers no viable destination within 10 km. Do not send supply caravan this route.

documents.title: Clinical Note — Chronic Radiation Exposure, Patient #117
documents.author: Dr. Veli M. (Infirmary)
documents.text: Patient #117 — male, age 34. Presenting: persistent nausea, fatigue, hair loss (diffuse). Dosimeter reading: 3.8 Sv cumulative (unknown timeframe). Blood work: WBC 1,800/μL (critically low). Lymphocytes: 400/μL. Assessment: chronic radiation syndrome, likely Grade II. Plan: chelation course if agents available. Rest. Remove from all exterior duty. Prognosis: guarded. The patient asks when he can go back to work. I have told him to rest. He will not rest. They never rest until they cannot.

documents.title: Transport Manifest — Convoy 9, Route Delta
documents.author: Logistics Office, Transit Authority
documents.text: MANIFEST — CONVOY 9. Vehicle: Armored half-track (#AT-04). Driver: Pell, W. Escort: 2 personnel. Route: Delta (shelter gate → lock gate four → grange hall → return). Cargo: 200L filtered water (8 drums), 40 kg flour (4 sacks), 12 units iodine tablets (sealed), 1 crate medical supplies (marked RED). Departure: Day 130, 0530. ETA return: Day 133. STATUS: Convoy 9 did not return. Day 133 passed. Day 134 passed. Driver Pell, W. confirmed dead per infirmary register #45 (cardiac, Day 290 — delayed entry). Cargo status: unknown. Vehicle status: unknown. File open.

documents.title: The Currents — Circular No. 17, Distributed by Hand
documents.author: The Currents (anonymous collective)
documents.text: CIRCULAR 17 — TO ALL WHO READ AND DO NOT LOOK AWAY. The Weigher's ledger is not the ledger. What is weighed is not what is counted. The grain that enters the silo is not the grain that leaves the ration line. We do not say who takes the difference. We say the difference exists. The silo is at loc_grain_silo. Go and count the sacks. Count them at dawn and count them at dusk. The number changes. We do not say who moves the sacks. We say the sacks move. If you understand this, you have already begun. Pass this circular to someone who has not begun. Do not pass it to someone who has.

documents.title: Diary Fragment — Three Pages, Water-Damaged
documents.author: Unknown (handwriting matches no known shelter resident)
documents.text: Day 310 — The road south is closed. They say it is radiation but I think it is something else. The motel has three other residents now. The owner, if she was the owner, left the key on the counter and walked out. Nobody followed her. Day 312 — I tried to walk to the pumphouse today. Turned back at the bridge. The water under the bridge is the wrong colour. Not brown. Not green. A colour I do not have a name for. Day 315 — [water damage obscures most of the page. Legible fragment:] ...told me the archive has records from before. Before what. Before the number changed. Before the... [rest illegible]

documents.title: Equipment Fault Report — Shelter Main Hatch Hydraulic Actuator
documents.author: Maintenance Chief Orin T.
documents.text: FAULT REPORT FR-2-175. Equipment: Main hatch hydraulic actuator (port side). Severity: CRITICAL. Description: Actuator failed to achieve full extension during routine cycle test. Hatch closed to 80% travel then stalled. Manual override required — three personnel, 40 minutes. Root cause: hydraulic fluid contamination (particulate visible to naked eye). Fluid sample submitted to lab. Preliminary assessment: seal degradation in the primary cylinder. The seal is not in the spare parts inventory. The spare parts inventory was last updated Day 90. It is Day 175. Interim measure: hatch cycle limited to one opening per 6-hour period. Recommend: fabricate replacement seal from available rubber stock. This is not a permanent fix. Nothing here has a permanent fix.

documents.title: Evacuation Roster — Sector 4 Residents, Order 112
documents.author: Consolidation Authority (stamped)
documents.text: EVACUATION ORDER 112 — SECTOR 4. Effective: Day 285, 1200 hours. All residents of Sector 4 (allocations 4-A through 4-F) are to report to the transit staging area at the weighbridge by 1000 hours. Personal belongings: one bag per person, maximum 15 kg. Livestock: not permitted. Tools: permitted with Quartermaster approval. Residents: [47 names listed — 31 accounted for at staging. 16 marked ABSENT. Of the 31 present: 28 relocated to shelter quarters. 3 held at conscription office for assignment review.] This roster is final. Appeals were heard Day 283. The appeals were denied. STAMPED: Consolidation Authority, Sector 4. SIGNED: [illegible]. DATE: Day 284.

documents.title: Transcription — Wall Markings, Sub-Level 2 Access Corridor
documents.author: Unknown (multiple authors over time)
documents.text: [Transcribed Day 210 by request of the Duty Clerk. Original markings on concrete wall, sub-level 2 corridor between storage and quarters.] Item 1 (chalk, white): "THE AIR TASTES LIKE METAL AND NOBODY WILL SAY WHY." Item 2 (charcoal): "ROOM 7 HEARS YOU SLEEPING." Item 3 (scratched, no pigment): "I COUNTED 40 PIPES GOING IN AND 39 COMING OUT. WHERE DOES THE OTHER ONE GO." Item 4 (grease crayon, yellow): "IF YOU ARE READING THIS YOU ARE STANDING IN THE WRONG PLACE." Item 5 (pencil, faint): "my name is Sera and I was here and I mattered." Item 6 (nail-scratched, large): "THE WEIGHER KNOWS." [End transcription. 6 markings documented. Wall scheduled for repainting Day 220. Repainting did not occur.]

documents.title: Caravan Master's Route Ledger — Ice Road Run, Season 2
documents.author: Caravan Master Tess O.
documents.text: Day 300: Departed holdfast. 6 pack animals, 2 drivers. Cargo: 120 kg dried fish, 40 kg bone charcoal, 20L lamp oil. Destination: slate hollow. Day 303: Reached bridge seven. Ice passable. One animal went through — recovered the pack, lost 8 kg fish. Day 306: Slate hollow. Sold 80 kg fish, 30 kg charcoal. Bought back: 15 kg flour, 6 hides (uncured). Day 310: Departed slate hollow for return. Day 314: Ambush at the rail span. Not bandits — three armed men, demanded half the cargo. Gave them 20 kg fish and 10L oil. No shots fired. Day 318: Back at holdfast. Net profit: 4 hides, 12 kg flour, 10L lamp oil minus losses. The road is not worth the road. I will run it again anyway. There is no other work.

documents.title: Clinical Note — Pediatric Fever, Unknown Origin
documents.author: Nurse Aide Senna
documents.text: Patient: child, female, approx age 6. Brought in by mother from the allotments. Symptoms: fever (39.4°C), rash on forearms, mild confusion. No known radiation exposure. No recent travel outside settlement. Vet surgery is being used as overflow — infirmary is full. I am not a doctor. I am a nurse aide working in a building for animals because the building for people has no beds left. Applied cool compresses. Administered willow bark tea (the only antipyretic we have). Mother says the child was playing near the seed library and may have ingested something. I do not know what is in the seed library. Nobody tells me what is in the seed library. Child is resting. Fever has not broken. I will check again at midnight.

documents.title: Water Quality Field Report — Terrace Pumphouse Intake
documents.author: Water Technician Pell R.
documents.text: Sample taken: Day 162, 0800, intake pipe at terrace pumphouse. Colour: pale yellow-green (abnormal). Odour: faint metallic, sulphuric undertone. pH: 5.8 (acidic — normal range 6.5–7.2). Turbidity: high. Sediment: visible particulate, grey-black. Test strip (rad): 0.9 Bq/L gross beta (elevated but within emergency tolerance of 2.0). Recommendation: do not use this intake without additional filtration. Install secondary charcoal filter before the distribution manifold. If charcoal is unavailable, boil for 15 minutes minimum and allow sediment to settle. This water will make people sick. It is making people sick. Three cases of gastrointestinal distress reported in the last 5 days from this intake. The filter is needed yesterday.
